10.text: In folk-tales, cases of vendetta are described almost with as much detail

11.text: as the episode of actual life narrated above. Thus, for instance, in the tale

12.text: of “Violent-One Murdered” (Eˊrmeč ɪn tɪˊmyo), the man is performing violence

13.text: on his neighbors and robbing them of the products of their seal-hunt. They

14.text: feel annoyed at this, and finally kill him. I mentioned this tale because of

15.text: its description of a violent man among the Maritime people.¹ In the second

16.text: part of the tale it is said that the killed one left two wives. One of them

17.text: was with child, and soon brought forth male twins. The boys grew up quickly;

18.text: but the family suffered many hardships, and often they had nothing to eat.

19.text: The women, however, incited the boys to continual exercise, in order to

20.text: prepare them for revenge. They said to them, “Our hunger comes from

21.text: the fact that your father was killed by his enemies. While he was living,

22.text: we always had plenty. So you are bound to avenge his death, and make

23.text: the families of his murderers also repine and starve.” The boys obeyed.

24.text: They were running all the time, hauling large trunks of trees, and fencing

25.text: with spears. Thus they became strong and active men. One day they killed

26.text: ten wild reindeer-bucks, and fed the two old women, their mother and her

27.text: companion, who were almost starved to death. Then they had a quarrel

28.text: with their neighbors, who had killed a whale. The old woman said, “Your

29.text: father perished with many wounds in his body. Go now and repay that.”

30.text: They went, and had a fight with their neighbors. All the men were killed.

31.text: Everything that moved on the shore was exterminated. The young children

32.text: of the killed men were reduced to starving orphans.²

33.text: It is curious to note that the idea of blood-revenge appears even in con-

34.text: nection with hunting and fishing pursuits. Thus the Chukchee say that the trap-

35.text: ping of foxes, otters, etc., is influenced by the desire of blood-revenge on the

36.text: part of animals. One of the trappers told me that every time his traps catch

37.text: a fox, he sees the fox in a dream beforehand. The animal attacks the hunter,

38.text: and wants to hurt him.³ In speaking of foxes, he called them “avengers”
